newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Telebras still an ING buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Telebras still an ING buy.

text.p: -- ING Barings said it has reiterated its buy recommendation on Brazilian federal telecoms company Telebras $150 per ADR after the company's release of first quarter results earlier this week.
-- "We believe the company reported a good set of results," ING analysts Patrick Jurczak, Andrew Friedman and Vera Rossi wrote in a report issued Friday.
-- The analysts said first quarter usage was in line with expectations, except for cellular phones, and they urged investors to take advantage of dips in Telebras' price to buy shares.
-- "Results will be even better, we believe, going forward because rate rebalancing takes place during second quarter 1997, starting May 19," they wrote.
-- ING Barings also said line growth in the first three months was slow, but could be explained by potential new customers waiting for the price of lines to drop to $280 by July 1 from $1,050.
-- "We are maintaining our year-end price target of $150 and our buy rating," the analysts wrote. "Should Telebras reach our target, the potential total return would be 25.1 percent."

-- Telebras reported Wednesday a consolidated net profit of 691 million reais, or $2.02 per ADR, which took into account a 103 million real (69 million reais after tax) one-time write-off related to Embratel's telex plant, they said.
-- They added that "normalized earnings" were 759 million reais, or $2.22, roughly 11.2 percent below ING's forecast, but in line with the market's consensus forecast.
-- Telebras's ADR was up 2-1/4 at 123-1/2 in New York and its preferred share was up 1.81 percent at 132.35 reais in Sao Paulo at 1416 local time/1316 EDT.
